issue_context:
Issue #14: feat: integrate GPU safety monitoring into main supervisor loop

## Context

The supervisor loop reads GPU telemetry every ~100ms (`HardwareBridge::read_telemetry_force`) but does nothing with safety thresholds. Three dead methods exist on `HardwareBridge`:

- `check_firmware()` — placeholder, always returns `true`
- `check_rails(_telem)` — returns empty vec, does nothing
- `apply_emergency_brake(pct)` — **real implementation**: calls `sudo nvidia-smi -pl` to set power limit

Additionally, `models.rs` defines a `FaultClass` enum that is never referenced from `main.rs`.

`is_gpu_healthy()` is already wired (called from `read_nvidia_smi()`), but higher-level safety decisions are missing.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Prune true stubs** from `src/gpu.rs`:
  - Remove `check_firmware()` (always returns true)
  - Remove `check_rails()` (returns empty vec)
- [ ] **Add `check_safety(telemetry: &GpuTelemetry)`** in `src/gpu.rs`:
  - Returns a `SafetyStatus` enum: `Ok`, `Warn(String)`, `Critical(String)`
  - `gpu_temp_c > 85.0` → thermal warning
  - `power_w > 350.0` → power critical (near RTX 5080 TDP of 360W)
- [ ] **Wire into main loop** in `src/main.rs`:
  - After telemetry read, call `check_safety()`
  - `Critical` → `apply_emergency_brake(0.5)` + log FATAL
  - `Warn` → log warning
  - Rate-limit check (every ~10 steps, not every 100ms iteration)
- [ ] **Clean up `src/models.rs`**:
  - Remove unused `FaultClass` enum or repurpose as `SafetyStatus`
- [ ] **Update docs**:
  - README "Safety Features": describe actual monitoring behavior
  - AGENTS.md: note 

Issue #12: chore: integrate safety stubs or prune dead code in gpu.rs

## Context

`src/gpu.rs` contains several methods that are never called from `main.rs`, the telemetry loop, or anywhere else in the crate:
- `HardwareBridge::apply_emergency_brake(pct)` — implements a real (sudo nvidia-smi -pl) power limit "CLOSED LOOP CONTROL: The Emergency Brake".
- `HardwareBridge::check_firmware()` — returns `true` with comment "Placeholder for CRC validation".
- `HardwareBridge::check_rails(_telem)` — returns empty vec.

`is_gpu_healthy()` and the nvidia-smi hung path are used, but the higher-level safety APIs are dead code.

Per the architecture in README and closed #2, emergency brakes / safety mechanisms are supposed to be part of the supervisor.

## Options (choose one in the issue or PR)
A. Integrate: Call `apply_emergency_brake` from the main loop or a new safety monitor when telemetry exceeds thresholds (temp, power, fan, etc.). Respect the existing "nvidia-smi hung" guard. Add logging + rate limiting.
B. Prune: Delete the unused methods (and any related dead imports/tests) to keep the API surface small and honest. Update README "Safety Features" if it over-promises.

## Tasks
- [ ] Audit all call sites of the three methods.
- [ ] Decide A or B (or hybrid: keep the brake but mark as internal + wire a minimal trigger).
- [ ] If integrating, add a simple policy in the 100 ms loop (e.g. if gpu_temp_c > X or power_w > Y).
- [ ] Ensure `cargo test` + clippy still pass.
- [ ] Update any docs that mention "Emergency Brakes" or "Safety Features".

## Vali

- **Removed dead stubs** from `src/gpu.rs`: `check_firmware()` (always returned true) and `check_rails()` (returned empty vec)
- **Added `SafetyStatus` enum** (`Ok`, `Warn`, `Critical`) and `HardwareBridge::check_safety(telemetry)` method
  - Thermal threshold: GPU temp >85°C → Critical
  - Power threshold: >350W (RTX 5080 TDP=360W) → Critical
  - Skips checks on simulated values (software-only mode)
- **Wired into main loop** with rate limiting: safety check runs every ~1 second (every 10 steps at 100ms)
  - Critical → `apply_emergency_brake(0.5)` + stderr log
  - Warn → stderr log
- **Removed `FaultClass` enum** from `src/models.rs` and the `models` module (never referenced from main)
- **Updated README** Safety Features section with actual monitoring behavior

review_signals.comment:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat simulated post-release telemetry as unsafe**

When the release task finishes after telemetry has fallen back to simulated idle values, `check_safety` returns `Ok` with `is_sim == true`; this block ignores that flag and only re-brakes on `Critical`, so it accepts the release, clears `brake_applied`, and subsequent simulated-Ok readings will no longer hold the brake. In a recovery where NVML/nvidia-smi drops out while `release_emergency_brake()` is in flight, this can restore the default power limit without real GPU readings, contradicting the earlier `is_sim` hold path.

review_signals.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
review_signals.comment:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fix the misspelled release safety arm**

This new arm references `SafetyStatys` and `is_sim`, neither of which exists in this scope (the enum is `SafetyStatus` and the bool was bound as `ism_`). As a result any `cargo build --bin thalamic-relay` fails before the relay can run, so the release-handler hardening cannot be shipped.

review_signals.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
review_signals.comment:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reapply the brake on post-release critical telemetry**

Once the new release handler compiles, the critical revalidation path won't reapply the brake in the normal case: after a completed release task there usually is no pending `brake_task`, so this `is_some()` guard skips spawning the emergency brake even though `release_emergency_brake()` has just restored the default power limit. That leaves `brake_applied` true while hardware is unthrottled, and later critical safety checks will also skip braking.

review_signals.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
review_signals.comment:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile state after ignoring a stale release**

Fresh evidence is the new stale-release arm: after `release_emergency_brake()` succeeds, simulated Ok or Warn telemetry reaches this branch, but it only logs and leaves `brake_applied` true without reapplying the power cap. In a dropout or warming GPU after a release, the hardware is already back at the default limit while the state says the brake is held, so subsequent Critical checks are suppressed by `if !brake_applied`.
